advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a chunk_by_facet test with >=2 distinct facets asserting no chunk contains criteria from more than one facet (facet purity), covering a count where a facet boundary falls mid-chunk.
evidence: tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:625: `crits = [{"id": f"C{i}", "facet": "ac-text-quality"} for i in range(count)]` — every criterion shares one facet, so multi-facet packing is never exercised
tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:611-612: existing test asserts only `sorted(flat) == sorted(...)` (completeness) and sizes, not per-chunk facet purity
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:519-520: comment claims 'Facet adjacency is preserved because the split stays contiguous over the facet-ordered list' — an untested behavioral claim
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:521-528: k/base/extra split runs over the whole `ordered` list ignoring facet boundaries, so a chunk can contain two facets
advisory.finding: The chunk_by_facet regression tests do not verify facet purity of the emitted chunks. The new balanced-packing algorithm splits the entire facet-ordered list into k near-equal contiguous chunks and can straddle facet boundaries, yet the new regression test (test_chunk_by_facet_never_strands_a_singleton) uses a single facet for all criteria, and the pre-existing multi-facet test (test_chunk_by_facet_packs_and_never_empty_for_input) asserts only chunk sizes and set-completeness. No test asserts that criteria of different facets are not mixed into the same chunk — the core contract implied by the function name and the new comment 'Facet adjacency is preserved'. A regression in the packing math that mixes facets would go undetected.
scenarios: A future edit to the k/base/extra computation reorders or regroups criteria such that two facets land in one chunk while all size/completeness assertions still pass
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a multi-facet case: build criteria across two facets (e.g. 5 of facet A, 4 of facet B) and assert `len({c['facet'] for c in ch}) == 1` for every returned chunk, plus set-completeness.
